- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < 0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > 0.2) after a downtrend, model underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 2–4 days to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply 1–2% downward adjustment to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to ignore sentiment and forecasts flat; apply 1–3% downward bias to all forecasts if sentiment avg < -0.1 over last 5 days.
